conventions.convention: Index sets are finite, nonempty and totally ordered. Balanced binary trees split ordered clusters into floor/ceiling halves and stop at the declared leaf threshold.

Admissibility requires strictly positive distance and distance ≥ η times the larger diameter. Repeated geometric points are permitted. Block recursion splits one eligible nonleaf cluster at a time, resolving cardinality ties on the row side.
Far blocks store UV* with rank bounded by an assumed cap; near blocks remain dense. Geometric admissibility alone supplies no low-rank guarantee.

Core-SVD uses absolute Frobenius tolerance, selects the smallest feasible integer rank including zero, and returns tolerance-not-met if no rank within the cap meets that tolerance. Empty factors and zero represented matrices return rank zero.

Bottom-up recompression adds all nodewise discarded-tail bounds within a factor-sum tree. Failure concerns the chosen tree and local budgets, not impossibility of approximating the exact full sum at the requested rank.
H² bases satisfy child restriction = child basis times child-to-parent transfer. Only leaf bases are stored explicitly; internal bases are reconstructed through transfers.

The complexity theorem uses leaf threshold b=k and explicit bounds on far side-size sums per block-tree level, total near blocks, and total H² couplings. These are additional assumptions, not consequences of admissibility.
The LU certificate assumes supplied exact factors A=LU, successful compression, exact arithmetic and exact norms. The inverse conclusion additionally requires ||A⁻¹||₂η<1.

load_bearing.statement: Let I,J be nonempty finite index sets with finite cluster trees, and construct the block-cluster tree as in def-hlr-cluster-trees-and-geometric-admissibility. Its terminal rectangles are pairwise disjoint and their union is I×J.

On success at rank q, the returned matrix has rank q and Frobenius residual equal to the singular-value tail at q, at most δ; no lower-rank matrix meets that tolerance. On tolerance-not-met, no matrix of rank at most k meets the tolerance.

Whenever all calls in a subtree succeed, its returned matrix has rank at most k and Frobenius error at most the reported sum of discarded-tail norms over that subtree, bounded by the sum of its node tolerances.

Disjoint block residual bounds δ_b give assembled Frobenius error at most (Σ_b δ_b²)¹ᐟ². Successful addition and product of approximations satisfy the stated input-perturbation bounds plus this output-compression budget.
H² far blocks are U_τ S_τσ V_σ*, with nested row and column cluster bases of ranks at most k; near blocks remain dense, and explicit basis storage is restricted to leaves.
For n≥1 and integer 1≤b≤n, cluster sizes at depth h are at most ceil(n/2^h); depth is at most ceil(log₂(n/b)), with at most 2n/b leaves and 4n/b−1 nodes.

For samples x_i∈[0,a], y_j∈[b,b+c], 0≤a<b, c≥0, and integer r≥1, the r-term geometric expansion has rank at most r, entrywise error at most (a/b)^r/(b−a), and Frobenius error at most √(mn) times that bound. The stated additional separation and cap hypotheses make it a permitted far-block representation.

published_dependencies.used_for: External batch-10 draft supplier: finite real/complex matrix rank, conjugate transpose and entrywise Frobenius norm conventions.
External batch-10 draft supplier: optimality and exact tail error of truncated SVD, including rank zero; also the Frobenius singular-value identity used in the inverse certificate.
Existence of compact singular decompositions and lifting the core SVD through orthonormal factors.
Frobenius and vector triangle inequalities and entrywise derivations of product-norm bounds. The modulus inequality remains valid under the conjugate-first Frobenius convention.
Maximum unit-vector stretch, operator submultiplicativity and inverse perturbation estimates; interpretation of the identity-block example.
The spectral norm is at most the Frobenius norm in the factorization certificate.
Every rank-at-most-one approximation of I₂ has operator-norm error at least one.
Injectivity of the compressed square matrix implies its image has dimension n.
An n-dimensional image subspace of the n-dimensional coordinate space is the whole space.
Converting bijectivity of the compressed matrix action into matrix invertibility.

concerns.concern: The input supplies exact matrix factors L,U, while the Procedure says to “apply [[alg-hlr-core-svd-recompression-with-tolerance]]” to each admissible block without specifying the factor-list input required by that routine. For a dense m_b×n_b block D, the exact pair (D,I_n_b) closes this immediately, as already specified in the bottom-up routine. The conversion should be explicit here to make the procedure executable from its declared inputs.
